title: Prefetch orchestration and safety slate for KV/prefix hit tuning
creator: Asha Patel
description: Deliver an operational playbook and automation for safe, measurable application of prefix/KV caching recommendations. This covers hit-rate modeling, adaptive TTL tuning, cache-key shaping heuristics, and a gated apply/rollback flow that avoids cost regressions and latency surprises.
background: We have existing heuristics for TTL and prefix caching but lack an automated, safety-first pipeline to propose, simulate, and apply changes across fleet slices. Previous manual rollouts caused noisy tail latency on a small cohort and missed opportunity to capture stable hit uplift. Goal: reduce token spend while maintaining p99 latency and error SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Automated recommendation engine outputs per-prefix TTL and prefetch policy with expected hit uplift and cost delta. 2) Simulation harness validates no >5% increase in p99 latency and <0.1% increase in error rate across target slices. 3) Staged rollout with shadow canary + automatic rollback on safety triggers. 4) Runbook + dashboard for ops and postmortem template.
notes: 2026-01-30: Kickoff. Defined scope to include model-level default TTLs, per-customer opt-outs, and a lightweight prefetch orchestrator. Stakeholders: Runtime, Console, Observability.

2026-02-07: Prototyped hit-rate estimator using stratified sampling from request traces (prefix, seq_len, model_variant). Initial result: median uplift 12% for heavy prefixes with 30% coverage of requests.
2026-02-18: Design review with PM/Design. Decided to separate cache-key shaping rules from TTL autosuggests to minimize blast radius; shaping rules require opt-in per-team.
2026-02-25: Implemented simulation harness that replays historical traffic with proposed TTLs and prefetch behavior; added KV miss penalty modeling (cpu + host queueing).

2026-03-04: Safety gate implemented: if simulated p99 latency increases by >3% or simulated error rate >0.05%, candidate is rejected. Ops asked for a stricter initial live gate (p99 +1% / error +0.02%).

2026-03-10: Ran shadow canary across 2% of production traffic in us-west: observed token cost down 8%, miss-rate down 18%, p99 latency up 0.6% (within live gate). Minor increase in host CPU on a small subset — mitigated by early throttling policy. Preparing PRs.
2026-03-11: Security & privacy check: no request payload is stored beyond existing trace retention. KMS used for config signing. No additional data classification required.
2026-03-12: In Review. Docs and runbook attached; request final sign-off from Runtime leads and SRE.
rollout_plan: Generate recommendations weekly via batch job that outputs candidate set + simulation metrics.
Shadow apply to 0.5% traffic for 48h with full tracing (no live caching); compute delta metrics.
Canary apply to 2% traffic for 24h with both shadow and live cache; enable lightweight throttling in the prefetch orchestrator.
Staged ramp to 10% / 25% / 50% with automated health checks at each step; 15-minute hold window per stage.
Full fleet apply with monitoring and 1-hour rollback window if live gates trip.
Automated rollback triggers: p99 latency increase >1% (live) or error rate increase >0.02% or CPU burst >30% for 5m sustained.
Post-apply 7-day observation period with cost & quality delta report.
Manual override: ops CLI command 'prefetch:disable <cohort>' and console toggle exposed to SREs and runtime oncall.
simulation_results_summary: median predicted token savings per model: 9%
heavy-prefix cohort (top 5% prefixes) predicted hit uplift: 22%
aggregate simulated p99 latency delta: +0.4% (main driver: slight increase in host CPU due to prefetch)
false-positive rate for prefix lift detection: 2.8% (we adopted conservative thresholds to reduce this)
recommended global baseline TTL change: +10% with per-prefix adjustments where model_seq_len > 128
testing_plan: Unit tests for recommendation scoring and TTL arithmetic
Integration test: simulation harness with synthetic traffic generator (edge cases: bursty prefixes, cold-start model variants)
Load test: apply prefetch agent in k8s staging cluster to validate CPU/IO impact at 10x traffic
Chaos test: force cache eviction and verify graceful behavior and rollback path
E2E smoke in canary: validate retrieval correctness and no degraded response bodies
runbook_snippets: To abort a rollout: run 'infra prefetched rollback --cohort <id> --reason <note>'
To throttle prefetching: echo '0' > /sys/rw/prefetch/agent_rps on the node pool (ops only)
To inspect simulated candidate: CLI 'prefetch inspect <candidate_id>' returns summary + link to replay notebook
Alerting: PagerDuty if p99 latency spike or error rate threshold breached; auto-rollback only if live gate breached
open_questions: Should default TTL suggestions be surfaced in Console for self-serve teams or remain an SRE-only feature initially?
Is per-customer opt-out necessary for EU tenants due to stricter data residency rules? (legal input pending)
Do we want cache-key shaping enabled by default for new models, or opt-in after validation?
reviews_and_feedback: PM (Lina Zhou): prefer exposing a confidence score and recommended confidence threshold in Console
SRE (Markus Olsson): requested a faster kill switch and an additional host CPU soft-limit to avoid noisy neighbor issues
Design (Rhea Singh): UX for rollout progress should include expected cost delta and an explicit 'safety margin' toggle
Runtime (Kunal Rao): suggested tighter canary duration for high-QPS models; added a model_variants exclusion list
postmortem_template: If rollout fails, populate: summary, timeline, root cause (hot path), detection, blast radius, corrective action, follow-ups (owners + due dates). Add cost & quality delta table for 7/30 day windows.

PM decision on Console visibility for suggestions (due 2026-03-16)
